subject.title: [Bug]: iOS app fails to connect over Tailscale CGNAT (100.x.x.x) — wss:// required but WebSocket upgrade silently dropped

question: Should iOS remote Gateway pairing support direct Tailscale CGNAT/plain `ws://` as a trusted local-network case, or should OpenClaw keep Tailscale mobile pairing on `wss://`/Serve and fix the native TLS diagnostics and proof path instead?
rationale: The code change is not only mechanical: it decides whether Tailscale CGNAT and MagicDNS are treated as plaintext-local for mobile bootstrap auth, or whether the supported mobile path remains secure WebSocket with better diagnostics and setup-code route selection.

options.title: Keep Secure WSS/Serve Path
options.body: Preserve the current plaintext fail-closed boundary, fix iOS TLS/reachability messages and trust-prompt behavior, and require real iOS Tailscale Serve/direct-WSS proof before closing.

options.title: Allow Direct Tailnet Plaintext
options.body: Treat Tailscale CGNAT and `.ts.net` as trusted local-network hosts for iOS manual/setup-code paths, with explicit tests and documentation for the security tradeoff.

options.title: Defer to Public WSS Guidance
options.body: Leave direct CGNAT unsupported and steer users to LAN, Tailscale Serve, SSH tunnel, or advanced public `wss://` setup until broader mobile pairing direction is settled.

recommendation.title: Keep Secure WSS/Serve Path
recommendation.body: Preserve the current plaintext fail-closed boundary, fix iOS TLS/reachability messages and trust-prompt behavior, and require real iOS Tailscale Serve/direct-WSS proof before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the merged route-list work and is the strongest current owner for the mobile pairing route contract and security decision.
